text: Glasspad puts your Mac's controls on your iPhone.
In the morning, it follows you from app to app.
Open Safari, and the buttons change to match.
The things you do every day stay pinned.
Split the phone itself, and keep two tools open at once.
In Final Cut, the edits you make most sit under your thumb.
On stage, it moves your slides, keeps time, and points for you.
On the couch, it becomes a remote.
Swipe to skip. Type to search.
Copy on your phone. Paste on your Mac.
Send a window to the other display, without reaching for it.
Keyboard, media, your Dock and macros are a tap away.
And under it all, a trackpad you can feel.
No account. No cloud. It all stays on your Wi-Fi.
